ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, for the inscribed quadrilateral $ABCD$ in the circle $\odot O$, if $\angle BCD=130^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$, \\
thus $\angle A = 180^\circ - \angle C = 50^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle BOD = 2\angle A = \boxed{100^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center marked as O; the four points A, B, C, D are on the circumference, forming the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD. It can be seen in the figure that B is at the upper left, C is on the left side, D is at the lower left, and A is at the lower right; line segments are connected from O to B and D, therefore ∠BOD is the central angle formed by OB and OD. The problem gives ∠BCD = 130°. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, one pair of opposite angles is supplementary, namely ∠DAB + ∠BCD = 180°. Therefore ∠DAB = 180° − 130° = 50°. ∠DAB is the inscribed angle subtending arc BD, while ∠BOD is the central angle subtending the same arc BD; the central angle subtending the same arc is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle, so ∠BOD = 2 × 50° = 100°.
